title: Divide Array Into Equal Pairs
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if the array can be partitioned into pairs of equal values.
Idea: Count each value with a frequency map and require all counts to be even.
Technique and why it applies: Even frequency for every value is necessary and sufficient for equal-value pairing.
Invariant: Frequency buckets account for every occurrence; each bucket can be paired only if its count is even.
Edge cases: An odd count makes pairing impossible; Java's fixed count array relies on bounded values.
Complexity: O(n+U) time, O(U) space.
complexity_reason: Even frequency for every value is necessary and sufficient for equal-value pairing.

Complexity: O(n+U) time, O(U) space.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public boolean divideArray(int[] nums){int[] c=new int[501];for(int x:nums)c[x]++;for(int x:c)if(x%2!=0)return false;return true;} }
complexity_reason: Even frequency for every value is necessary and sufficient for equal-value pairing.

title: Count Hills and Valleys in an Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Count interior positions that are hills or valleys after consecutive equal values are treated as one run.
Idea: Collapse consecutive equal values, then count interior values larger than both neighbors or smaller than both.
Technique and why it applies: Removing duplicates makes each candidate compare against nearest distinct values.
Invariant: After compression, neighbors are the nearest distinct values.
Edge cases: Only interior runs count; a plateau is one run.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for compressed values.
complexity_reason: Removing duplicates makes each candidate compare against nearest distinct values.

title: Count Hills and Valleys in an Array
notes:
Task and constraints: Count interior positions that are hills or valleys after consecutive equal values are treated as one run.
Idea: Collapse consecutive equal values, then count interior values larger than both neighbors or smaller than both.
Technique and why it applies: Removing duplicates makes each candidate compare against nearest distinct values.
Invariant: After compression, neighbors are the nearest distinct values.
Edge cases: Only interior runs count; a plateau is one run.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for compressed values.
code: class Solution { public int countHillValley(int[] nums){int ans=0;for(int i=1;i<nums.length-1;i++){if(nums[i]==nums[i-1])continue;int l=i-1,r=i+1;while(l>=0&&nums[l]==nums[i])l--;while(r<nums.length&&nums[r]==nums[i])r++;if(l>=0&&r<nums.length&&((nums[i]>nums[l]&&nums[i]>nums[r])||(nums[i]<nums[l]&&nums[i]<nums[r])))ans++;}return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Removing duplicates makes each candidate compare against nearest distinct values.

title: Find the Difference of Two Arrays
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the distinct values present only in nums1 and only in nums2.
Idea: Convert both arrays to sets and return each set difference.
Technique and why it applies: Set difference directly produces unique values exclusive to each array.
Invariant: Each result contains unique values present on one side only.
Edge cases: Duplicates disappear; common values appear in neither result.
Complexity: O(n+m) expected time and O(n+m) space.
complexity_reason: Set difference directly produces unique values exclusive to each array.

Invariant: Each result contains unique values present on one side only.
Edge cases: Duplicates disappear; common values appear in neither result.
Complexity: O(n+m) expected time and O(n+m) space.
code:
import java.util.*;
class Solution { public List<List<Integer>> findDifference(int[] nums1,int[] nums2){Set<Integer>a=new HashSet<>(),b=new HashSet<>();for(int x:nums1)a.add(x);for(int x:nums2)b.add(x);Set<Integer>x=new HashSet<>(a);x.removeAll(b);Set<Integer>y=new HashSet<>(b);y.removeAll(a);return Arrays.asList(new ArrayList<>(x),new ArrayList<>(y));} }
complexity_reason: Set difference directly produces unique values exclusive to each array.

title: Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the number of bit positions where start and goal differ.
Idea: Count set bits in `start ^ goal` with `bit_count` or `Integer.bitCount`.
Technique and why it applies: XOR marks the differing positions and population count totals them.
Invariant: XOR has a set bit exactly where the input bits differ.
Edge cases: Equal inputs yield zero; no binary strings are needed.
Complexity: O(1) time and space for fixed-width integers.
code:
class Solution:
 def minBitFlips(self,start,goal):return (start^goal).bit_count()
complexity_reason: XOR marks the differing positions and population count totals them.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Convert Time
notes:
Task and constraints: Convert current time to correct time using increments of 60, 15, 5, and 1 minute; return the minimum operation count.
Idea: Convert times to minutes and greedily use increments 60, 15, 5, then 1.
Technique and why it applies: Taking the largest permitted increment first minimizes operations for these denominations.
Invariant: The remaining difference tracks minutes not yet covered after each quotient and remainder.
Edge cases: Correct time is not earlier than current time.
Complexity: O(1) time and space.
complexity_reason: Taking the largest permitted increment first minimizes operations for these denominations.

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Convert Time

Technique and why it applies: Taking the largest permitted increment first minimizes operations for these denominations.
Invariant: The remaining difference tracks minutes not yet covered after each quotient and remainder.
Edge cases: Correct time is not earlier than current time.
Complexity: O(1) time and space.
code: class Solution { public int convertTime(String current,String correct){String[]a=current.split(":"),b=correct.split(":");int d=(Integer.parseInt(b[0])*60+Integer.parseInt(b[1]))-(Integer.parseInt(a[0])*60+Integer.parseInt(a[1]));int ans=0;for(int step:new int[]{60,15,5,1}){ans+=d/step;d%=step;}return ans;} }
complexity_reason: Taking the largest permitted increment first minimizes operations for these denominations.

title: Add Two Integers
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the sum of num1 and num2.
Idea: Return `num1 + num2` directly, without loops, helper structures, or conversions.
Technique and why it applies: Integer addition is the exact operation requested and handles positive, negative, and zero operands naturally.
Invariant: The returned result equals the mathematical sum of the two input values.
Edge cases: Adding zero preserves the other operand; negative operands use ordinary signed addition; no array or null handling is involved.
Complexity: O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space for fixed-size integer inputs.
code:
class Solution:
 def sum(self,num1,num2):return num1+num2
complexity_reason: Direct integer addition returns the required sum in constant time and constant auxiliary space.

title: Root Equals Sum of Children
notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if the root value equals the sum of its two children.
Idea: Compare `root.val` with `root.left.val + root.right.val`.
Technique and why it applies: The property concerns only the root and its immediate children.
Invariant: The result checks the root against its two immediate children.
Edge cases: The problem guarantees both children; deeper descendants are irrelevant.
Complexity: O(1) time and space.
code:
class Solution:
 def checkTree(self,root):return root.val==root.left.val+root.right.val
complexity_reason: The property concerns only the root and its immediate children.

title: Find Closest Number to Zero
approach_name: Minimize absolute value and prefer positive ties
notes:
Task and constraints: Return the array value closest to zero; if tied, return the larger value.
Idea: Choose the value with minimum absolute value; on ties choose the larger value.
Technique and why it applies: Distance first and larger-value tie breaking implement the stated rule.
Invariant: The candidate is best by distance, then by numeric value.
Edge cases: For equal magnitudes choose the positive value; Java widens before absolute value.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space.
code:
class Solution:
 def findClosestNumber(self,nums):return max(nums,key=lambda x:(-abs(x),x))
complexity_reason: Distance first and larger-value tie breaking implement the stated rule.

code: class Solution { public int findClosestNumber(int[] nums){int best=nums[0];for(int x:nums)if(Math.abs((long)x)<Math.abs((long)best)||(Math.abs((long)x)==Math.abs((long)best)&&x>best))best=x;return best;} }

title: Calculate Digit Sum of a String
notes:
Task and constraints: Partition the digit string into groups of k, replace each group with its digit sum, and repeat until length is at most k.
Idea: While length exceeds k, sum each consecutive group of up to k digits and concatenate group sums.
Technique and why it applies: Repeated group summation follows the required transformation until the length threshold.
Invariant: Each pass produces the next string; stop when its length is at most k.
Edge cases: The final group can be shorter; regroup on each iteration.
Complexity: O(L log L) upper-bound time and O(L) temporary space.
complexity_reason: Repeated group summation follows the required transformation until the length threshold.

title: Calculate Digit Sum of a String
notes:
Task and constraints: Partition the digit string into groups of k, replace each group with its digit sum, and repeat until length is at most k.
Idea: While length exceeds k, sum each consecutive group of up to k digits and concatenate group sums.
Technique and why it applies: Repeated group summation follows the required transformation until the length threshold.
Invariant: Each pass produces the next string; stop when its length is at most k.
Edge cases: The final group can be shorter; regroup on each iteration.
Complexity: O(L log L) upper-bound time and O(L) temporary space.
code: class Solution { public String digitSum(String s,int k){while(s.length()>k){StringBuilder b=new StringBuilder();for(int i=0;i<s.length();i+=k){int sum=0;for(int j=i;j<Math.min(s.length(),i+k);j++)sum+=s.charAt(j)-'0';b.append(sum);}s=b.toString();}return s;} }
complexity_reason: Repeated group summation follows the required transformation until the length threshold.

title: Count Prefixes of a Given String
notes:
Task and constraints: Count words that are prefixes of s.
Idea: Count words satisfying `s.startswith(w)` or `s.startsWith(w)`.
Technique and why it applies: The starts-with predicate directly tests the required prefix condition.
Invariant: Every word is tested independently and every match adds one.
Edge cases: A word equal to s is a prefix; duplicate words count separately.
Complexity: O(total characters examined) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
code:
class Solution:
 def countPrefixes(self,words,s):return sum(s.startswith(w) for w in words)
complexity_reason: The starts-with predicate directly tests the required prefix condition.
